name: Yongbei Zhuang
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Zhang Junru et al. 1999. Zhuangyu fangyan yanjiu [A study of Zhuang dialects]. Chengdu: Sichuan Minzu Chubanshe — dialect phonologies incl. Yongbei Zhuang; not online

sources.citation: Perkins, Jeremy, Seunghun J. Lee & Julian Villegas. 2016. An interplay between F0 and phonation in Du'an Zhuang tone. Proceedings of TAL 2016, Buffalo (ISCA archive).
sources.note: Not Yongbei (Du'an = Hongshui He Zhuang) and silent on stress: acoustic study of the six unchecked tones of one speaker, creak on two tones. (Semantic Scholar mis-titles it 'Wuming Zhuang'.)

sources.citation: Pittayaporn, Pittayawat. 2009. The Phonology of Proto-Tai. PhD dissertation, Cornell University (eCommons 1813/13855). 438 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on Zhuang stress; comparative reconstruction with general remarks on sesquisyllables and the Proto-Tai prosodic word (ch. 2); no statement about Wuming/Yongbei Zhuang word stress.

sources.citation: Luo, Yongxian. 2008. Zhuang. In A. V. N. Diller, J. A. Edmondson & Y. Luo (eds), The Tai-Kadai Languages (Routledge Language Family Series), 317-377. London: Routledge.
sources.note: Silent. Grep of the scanned text of pp. 317-377 finds no 'stress', 'accent', 'prominence' or 'unstressed'; the book index (p. 682) lists 'stress' only on Thai/Lao/Shan/Lue/Tai-aesthetics/Chadong pages (34, 86, 118, 124, 158, 162, 184, 292, 293, 411, 534, 600), none in the Zhuang chapter. 9.2 gives N/S Zhuang initial and rhyme correspondences, six-dialect tone table (Wuming 24 31 55 42 35 33), and a Fengshan Zhuang segment/tone sketch; 9.3.2: 'The majority of words in Zhuang are monosyllabic... Disyllabic words are not uncommon' (pp. 324-325). Source: user-uploaded copy in the archive.org 'ope…

sources.citation: SIL Notes on Linguistics 1996 (ERIC ED401726), incl. an article assessing Zhuang dialect intelligibility from sound correspondences (Wuming vs Wenshan, Long'an, Yishan/Donglan, S. Laibin/Nandan; data from Wei & Qin 1980).
sources.note: Nothing on Zhuang stress; the word 'stress' occurs only in unrelated articles in the issue.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Standard Zhuang' (en), 'Zhuang languages' (en), '壮语' / '標準壯語' (zh); Omniglot 'Zhuang'
sources.note: Tones and syllable structure only ('Zhuang words can be made up of one, two, or three syllables'); no mention of stress; cite Wei & Qin 1980, Zhang et al. 1999, Luo 2008, Burusphat et al. 2012.

sources.citation: 民族语文论集 (中国社会科学出版社; incl. 韦庆稳《越人歌》与壮语的关系试探) and 语言研究论丛 第七辑 (南开大学) -- Chinese paper collections from the same archive.org item
sources.note: Grep 重音/轻声/轻读 against 壮语: no Zhuang stress statement (重音 hits concern Mongolian and Chinese).

sources.citation: Snyder, Wil C. & Lu Tianqiao. 1997. Wuming Zhuang tone sandhi: a phonological, syntactic, and lexical investigation. In Jerold A. Edmondson & David B. Solnit (eds), Comparative Kadai: The Tai Branch (SIL/UTA Publications in Linguistics 124), 107-137. Dallas: SIL & UTA.

sources.note: Only English-language phonological study devoted to Wuming Zhuang; a tone-sandhi study of disyllables is where prominence/stress asymmetries between syllables would be discussed. Harvard print: WID Offsite PL4113.C56 1997; TOZ Offsite L.SOC.120.11.1.5.3 (124).

sources.citation: Moskalev, Aleksej A. 1971. Grammatika jazyka čžuan [Грамматика языка чжуан]. Moscow: Nauka (AN SSSR, Institut vostokovedenija). 336 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Only full reference grammar of (Wuming-based) Zhuang in a European language; Soviet Nauka grammars of this series normally contain an 'Ударение' subsection in the phonetics chapter, so it is the likeliest place for an explicit stress statement. Harvard print: WID Offsite Storage 1286.16.125 (Scan & Deliver).

sources.citation: Li, Fang-Kuei. 1965 [1956]. The Tai Dialect of Wuming (武鳴土語): texts, translations and glossary. BIHP Academia Sinica Monograph Series A 19. 301 pp. (reprint: 李方桂 2005 武鸣土语, 李方桂全集 4, 北京: 清华大学出版社); and Li 1947 武鳴土語音系 [Phonology of the Tai dialect of Wu-ming], BIHP 12: 293-303.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The classic primary phonological description of exactly the Wuming variety; the 1947 phonology article is the place to check for a statement on stress/prominence in disyllables. BIHP vol. 12 is on archive.org (item ihp-sinica) but in a logged-in-only collection.
